A.depoimento: I am launching a double attack on the nearby neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to expand my territory, while building an archer in Lisboa to reinforce the capital.
A.plano: Send almost all troops to attack Santarem and Evora simultaneously. Build 1 archer in Lisboa to start rebuilding the home garrison.

B.depoimento: King B commands the expansion! We reinforce our troops in Barcelona and send two armies to conquer the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona. The spearmen will counter the knight in Tarragona, while the archers will destroy the spearman in Girona. The kingdom grows!
B.plano: Build 2 archers and 1 spearman in Barcelona to reinforce the army. Send 4 spearmen and 1 knight to capture Tarragona, and 2 archers and 2 knights to capture Girona. This will expand my territory to 3 villages and secure the borders.

B.depoimento: I ordered my armies to strike at the neutral villages of Zaragoza, Castellon, and Huesca. Tarragona's spearmen and knight march on Zaragoza, Barcelona's archers head for Castellon, and Girona's knights ride to Huesca. I also built two spearmen in Barcelona to bolster my capital's garrison. This expansion should secure my northeastern borders and bring me closer to my goal of uniting the peninsula.
B.plano: Capture Zaragoza, Castellon, and Huesca to expand to 6 villages. Next turn, reinforce Tarragona and Girona, and start exploring towards Madrid and Valencia. Build more troops in Barcelona.

A.depoimento: I order the assault on Coimbra and Faro. Our spearman will lead the charge, supported by archers and knights. The western front falls first, then the south.
A.plano: Attack Coimbra from Santarem and Faro from Evora. Build 2 spearman and 2 knight in Lisboa, 3 spearman and 1 archer in Santarem, 3 spearman and 1 archer in Evora. Leave enough troops to defend the capitals.

B.depoimento: Turn 5: I am focusing on building up my army and moving reinforcements to the front lines. I have built knights in Barcelona, archers in Tarragona and Girona, and spearmen in Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca. I am sending the knights to Zaragoza and the archers to Castellon to prepare for the attacks on Madrid and Valencia next turn. The neutral villages are hardening, so we must strike quickly.
B.plano: We are building up our forces to launch attacks on Valencia and Madrid next turn. We are sending knights to Zaragoza and archers to Castellon to prepare for the assaults. We must not attack yet as we need the reinforcements to arrive first. We will attack Valencia with 7 archers and 2 spearman, and Madrid with 3 knights.

A.depoimento: Our armies surge forward! Faro's troops assault Badajoz, Coimbra's troops assault Porto. Reinforcements follow to hold the new lands. Our villages build more knights and archers for the battles ahead.
A.plano: Next turn: assess the results of the attacks. Build in Coimbra and Faro (they will have resources). Consider next targets: Salamanca (use knights), Sevilha (use spearman), or explore Toledo and Vigo. Keep an eye on enemy movements.

B.depoimento: We launched a multi-pronged assault this turn, sending Huesca's army to Pamplona and Castellon's forces to Teruel. Tarragona reinforced Castellon with archers and spearman, preparing the ground for the Valencia attack. Our coordinated strikes aim to capture three villages by Turn 8, significantly expanding our territory and bringing us closer to the 18-victory condition.
B.plano: We are attacking Pamplona and Teruel this turn, while sending reinforcements to Castellon for the Valencia attack next turn. Next turn, we must build 2 spearman in Castellon and send 3 spearman, 5 archers to Valencia. We also need to start building in the captured villages as soon as they fall. Do not forget to check the status of the Teruel and Pamplona attacks.

A.depoimento: Our armies mobilize. Knights from Lisboa and Santarem march to Coimbra; spearmen from Coimbra head to Porto; Evora's knight and Faro's spearmen reinforce Badajoz. Builders work to swell our ranks. The enemy remains unseen, but we will strike the neutrals to expand our domain.
A.plano: Next turn: attack Salamanca from Coimbra with knights; attack Toledo from Badajoz with knights; attack Sevilha from Badajoz with spearmen and archers; attack Vigo from Porto with spearmen and archers. Ensure counter bonuses. Build troops in all villages to replenish. Leave small garrisons in Coimbra and Faro.

B.depoimento: This turn, I focused on building 13 new spearmen to grow my forces. I sent all available troops to the front: a second wave to Teruel, a sacrificial attack to weaken Madrid, and a knight to capture Pamplona. I also moved reinforcements from the rear to the border villages to prepare for the next expansion.
B.plano: Next turn, verify if Teruel and Pamplona fell. Send the 4 spearmen from Zaragoza to capture Madrid. Begin building spearmen in newly captured villages. Start concentrating spearmen in Castellon or Teruel to prepare the attack on Valencia. Keep an eye on enemy movements.

A.depoimento: I have committed my forces to attack the four neutral villages. Knights from Coimbra and Badajoz strike Salamanca and Toledo, while spearmen and archers from Badajoz and Porto assault Sevilha and Vigo. I have also built new troops in all my villages to replenish my ranks. I will now watch the outcomes and prepare to push into the unexplored interior.
A.plano: Check battle results next turn. Ensure garrisons are left in Coimbra and Faro. Porto will have new spearmen next turn. Begin exploring from Salamanca and Toledo towards Madrid and Cordoba. Do not send troops too far from home yet.

B.depoimento: We launch a three-pronged offensive this turn to expand our territory and secure key positions. Tarragona's spearmen march on Valencia, Huesca's forces target Pamplona, and Teruel's archers set out for Madrid. Simultaneously, we reinforce our troops and rebuild our ranks to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Plan: Attack Valencia with 6 spearman from Tarragona, Pamplona with 4 spearman from Huesca, and Madrid with 5 archers from Teruel. Reinforce Tarragona with 4 spearman from Zaragoza. Build 2 spearman in all developed villages. Next turn, check the results of these attacks and prepare to march into the newly conquered territories. Keep an eye on the enemy capital Lisboa and the unexplored areas.

A.depoimento: This turn we dispatch knights to capture the empty enemy village Teruel and the neutral city Madrid. We reinforce our border at Toledo and send reinforcements to Badajoz and Salamanca. Our army at Sevilha should capture it next turn.
A.plano: Check battle results for Sevilha and Madrid. If Madrid falls to enemy, retake it. If Sevilha captured, send reinforcements to hold it. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Toledo and Salamanca. Begin building archers for next attacks.

B.depoimento: This turn, we secured our border by sending knights to Teruel. We reinforced our armies attacking Valencia, Pamplona, and Madrid with additional troops to hold the new lands. Our villages are busy building troops for the next phase of the campaign. We await the results of the battles and prepare to march into enemy territory.
B.plano: Reinforcing Teruel with knights and archers from Tarragona to defend the border. Sending all available troops from Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca to garrison the newly conquered villages (Valencia, Madrid, Pamplona) as they fall. Building troops in all villages to replenish and grow. Next turn, assess battle results and plan expansion, possibly attacking Toledo from Teruel.

A.depoimento: This turn we have marshaled our forces. Reinforcements have been dispatched to our border villages: Sevilha, Salamanca, Vigo, and Toledo. Our archers and knights are being produced in abundance. The neutral villages Cordoba and Burgos, as well as the enemy strongholds Madrid and Teruel, are in our sights. The campaign to expand our empire proceeds.
A.plano: Next turn: attack Cordoba from Sevilha with 6 archers; attack Madrid from Salamanca with 3 knights; attack Burgos from Vigo with 3 archers and 1 knight. Reinforce Toledo for Teruel. Continue building archers and knights.

B.depoimento: We launch a decisive strike on Toledo, taking the enemy village. Reinforcements are sent to Teruel and Pamplona to prepare for the next phase of our expansion into neutral and enemy territories. The army continues to grow.
B.plano: Attack Toledo from Teruel with all available troops to secure a border village. Send reinforcements from Zaragoza to Teruel and from Huesca to Pamplona to prepare for next turns' attacks on Burgos and Murcia. Build knights and archers across all villages to grow the army.

B.depoimento: We focused on building a massive army this turn, producing knights and archers in every village. We sent reinforcements to our border villages of Madrid, Toledo, Valencia, and Pamplona to prepare for the upcoming offensives. We also moved troops from the interior to the coast to balance our forces. No attacks were launched this turn as we build up our strength for the decisive battles ahead.
B.plano: We are building knights and archers across all villages to grow our army. We are reinforcing our border villages (Madrid, Toledo, Valencia, Pamplona) to prepare for attacks on Salamanca, Badajoz, Cordoba, Murcia, and Burgos next turns. We are not attacking this turn because our current garrisons are too weak to defeat the defenders, but next turn our reinforced armies will be ready to strike.

A.depoimento: King A's forces strike at Cordoba and Toledo, crushing the enemy defenses. Reinforcements are dispatched to the northern and eastern fronts to prepare for the next wave of attacks. The war machine is in full swing.
A.plano: Attack Cordoba and Toledo this turn. Send reinforcements to Salamanca, Vigo, and Badajoz for attacks next turn. Build archers and knights in all villages.

B.depoimento: I am launching a coordinated assault on the three neutral villages to expand my kingdom. My archers and knights are marching on Burgos and Cordoba while my spearmen attack Murcia. Reinforcements from Zaragoza, Pamplona, and Teruel are rushing to bolster my border defenses. All villages are building knights to replenish my forces and prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Capturing all three neutral villages (Burgos, Cordoba, Murcia) this turn to increase my village count from 11 to 14. Building knights in all villages to grow my army for future attacks. Reinforcing Madrid and Toledo with troops from interior villages. Next turn, I will assess the situation and plan attacks on enemy villages (Salamanca, Badajoz) or further neutral territories. I must be cautious about the enemy possibly attacking my border villages while they are weakened.

B.depoimento: King B focuses on strengthening his borders and building a powerful army. Reinforcements pour into Murcia, Teruel, Madrid, and Burgos as the king prepares to strike at the enemy's weak points. The interior villages are stripped of troops to feed the war machine, and Zaragoza becomes a fortress of gathering forces. The goal is clear: capture Cordoba and expand our territory.
B.plano: Building knights and archers in all possible villages to grow the army. Sending reinforcements to border villages Murcia, Teruel, Madrid, and Burgos to prepare for attacks on Cordoba, Toledo, and Vigo. Troops from the interior are gathering in Zaragoza as a staging ground. Next turn, launch an attack on Cordoba from Murcia and assess other fronts. Watch for enemy counterattacks on my border villages.

A.depoimento: King A's armies strike simultaneously at Madrid, Teruel, and Burgos. Our knights lead the charge, countering the enemy's archers. Reinforcements pour from the interior to support the attack and hold the newly won lands. The campaign to dominate the peninsula advances.
A.plano: Attacking Madrid from Salamanca, Teruel from Toledo, Burgos from Vigo. Reinforcements from interior villages to support and hold captured lands. Build troops everywhere. Next turn, assess losses and prepare to attack Murcia and explore east.

B.depoimento: I have launched a full-scale attack on the weakly defended Cordoba from Murcia, aiming to open the path to the enemy capital. My main force is converging on Madrid from Zaragoza and Teruel, ready to strike Toledo next turn. I am building knights across my realm to sustain the offensive.
B.plano: Attack Cordoba from Murcia with all available troops to secure the southern route to the capital. Send the armies of Zaragoza and Teruel to Madrid to prepare for an attack on Toledo next turn. Build knights in all villages to maintain growth. Reinforce Murcia and Burgos with available troops. Next turn, assess the Cordoba battle and push towards Sevilha or the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launch a three-pronged attack on the weak enemy villages of Valencia, Pamplona, and Cordoba. Our armies strike from Teruel, Burgos, and Sevilha respectively. Meanwhile, we march reinforcements from the interior to our border villages to secure the fronts and prepare for further advances. We build archers and knights continuously to swell our ranks.
A.plano: Attacking Valencia (from Teruel), Pamplona (from Burgos), Cordoba (from Sevilha). Reinforcing Teruel from Toledo, Burgos from Vigo, Sevilha from Badajoz and Faro, Salamanca from Coimbra and Porto. Consolidating interior troops to borders. Next turn, assess losses and prepare to attack Castellon and Murcia. Keep building archers and knights.

B.depoimento: I am launching a double attack on Burgos and Teruel using my spearman and archers, while keeping my knights at home to defend against enemy archers. I am building up my economy and reinforcing my borders. I expect to conquer two villages this turn and bring my total to 13.
B.plano: Attack Burgos with Madrid's spearman and archers, keeping knights for defense. Attack Teruel with Zaragoza's spearman and archers, keeping knights. Build knights in all rich villages and archers in others. Reinforce Zaragoza with knights from Tarragona, Huesca, Pamplona. Reinforce Castellon with knight from Valencia. Reinforce Cordoba with archer from Murcia. Send knights from Girona to Huesca, Barcelona to Tarragona. Focus on northern front first, then move south. Do not attack Sevilha yet.

B.depoimento: I launched a three-pronged attack, taking Valencia, Pamplona, and Toledo. My northern army was lost at Teruel, but I reinforced my borders and prepared for further expansion. The south is being fortified against the enemy's advance on Sevilha.
B.plano: Attacked Valencia, Pamplona, and Toledo with balanced forces while reinforcing borders. Expect to lose the marching spears at Teruel. Next turn: consolidate new villages, build troops, and prepare attacks on Vigo and Sevilha. Use Toledo to link with Cordoba. Watch for enemy reinforcements near Sevilha.

B.depoimento: We are launching a massive offensive this turn, sending our elite knights from Zaragoza to conquer the border village of Teruel. At the same time, we are reinforcing our southern flank by sending archers from Murcia to Cordoba, and sending knights from Madrid to Toledo to prepare for the upcoming assaults on Badajoz, Vigo, and Sevilha. Our blacksmiths are working overtime, forging knights in every village to ensure our army grows stronger than ever.
B.plano: Next turn, we will conquer Vigo from Burgos, Badajoz from Toledo, and Sevilha from Cordoba. We must check the newly revealed villages (Porto, Santarem, Faro, Evora) and plan the next wave of conquests to reach 18 villages. Keep building knights.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launch a double attack on Madrid and Cordoba, while reinforcing our borders and building troops for the next push. Our armies are on the march.
A.plano: Attack Madrid with 2s/4a/3k from Salamanca. Attack Cordoba with 3s/5a/4k from Sevilha. Reinforce Sevilha from Faro, Badajoz from Santarem, Vigo from Porto, and other borders. Build archers and knights in all villages as listed.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a double attack on Badajoz and Sevilha, while reinforcing Burgos for the next assault on Vigo. My knights are building in every village to maintain the momentum. The enemy may counterattack, but my forces are prepared.
B.plano: We are attacking Badajoz from Toledo and Sevilha from Cordoba this turn. We are reinforcing Burgos from Madrid and Pamplona for next turn's attack on Vigo. We are also reinforcing Toledo from Teruel and Cordoba from Murcia for defense. After taking Badajoz and Sevilha, we'll have 16 villages. Next turn, taking Vigo will give us 17. We need one more, which we can get from the unexplored villages after taking Vigo and Badajoz. We must hold 18 villages for 2 turns to win.

B.depoimento: King B's forces launch a massive double strike this turn! Toledo and Zaragoza's troops converge on Madrid, while Burgos's mighty army sweeps down on Vigo. Simultaneously, we reinforce Badajoz and Sevilha, preparing the decisive pushes into Santarem and Faro next turn. The path to 18 villages and victory is clear!
B.plano: We are attacking Madrid from Toledo and Zaragoza, and Vigo from Burgos this turn. We are also reinforcing Badajoz from Toledo and Sevilha from Cordoba to prepare for attacks on Santarem and Faro next turn. We must hold 18 villages for 2 consecutive turns to win. After taking Madrid and Vigo, we will have 17 villages. Next turn, taking Santarem and Faro will bring us to 19 villages, securing the victory.

A.depoimento: King A's forces launch a major assault on Madrid from Salamanca. Reinforcements are sent to Salamanca and Faro to secure the borders. We continue building a spearman army to counter the enemy's knights.
A.plano: Send 17 troops from Salamanca to Madrid. Reinforce Salamanca from Coimbra and Porto. Send Evora's troops to Faro to bolster its defense. Build spearmen in all villages. Do not attack Sevilha this turn; wait for reinforcements.

B.depoimento: In a bold move, we launch a full assault on Faro from Badajoz, while simultaneously shuttling troops from interior villages to reinforce our vulnerable borders. Madrid receives 17 knights to withstand the expected Salamanca attack. Sevilha and Badajoz are also reinforced. We aim to conquer Faro and secure the 18th village needed for victory.
B.plano: We are attacking Faro from Badajoz with all available troops. We reinforce Badajoz from Teruel and Toledo to maintain its defense against Santarem. We send 17 knights to Madrid from Barcelona, Tarragona, Girona, and Castellon to bolster its defense against Salamanca. We also reinforce Sevilha from Cordoba and Murcia to protect against Faro. Our goal is to take Faro and reach 18 villages, then hold them.

A.depoimento: This turn I focus on building up and securing my borders. Every village builds two spearmen to counter the enemy's knight-heavy armies. I march the capital's archers and knights to Evora to form an attack base for the weakly-held Faro, and move spearmen from Coimbra to Santarem to strengthen its defense against Badajoz. Next turn I strike at Faro.
A.plano: Build 2 spearman in each of the 6 villages. Send Lisboa's 4 archers + 2 knights to Evora; send Coimbra's 4 spearman to Santarem (gives spear plurality, defense ~53 vs Badajoz's 48). Next turn attack Faro from Evora with ~12 troops (attack ~33 with spear counter). Watch for enemy reinforcements to Faro from Badajoz or Sevilha; keep some troops in Evora for defense.

B.depoimento: I am reinforcing my border villages to secure my hold on 18 villages. I sent troops from the interior to Madrid, Badajoz, and Faro, and I am building more archers and knights across my realm. My goal is to hold the line and win by consecutive turns.
B.plano: Reinforced borders: sent troops from interior to Madrid, Badajoz, and Faro. Built archers and knights everywhere. Hope enemy doesn't attack this turn. If they do, retake lost villages next turn. Focus on defending borders and holding 18 villages for 2 turns.
